raw_case_text:
A 63-year-old Thai male farmer residing in central Thailand presented with prolonged fever and non-productive cough for 3 months. He also complained of intermittent chest tightness at the left hemithorax and losing 4 kg of his weight. He was admitted to the local hospital and diagnosed with bacterial pneumonia at that time. However, his fever did not subside following 14 days of intravenous meropenem. He was, therefore, transferred to our hospital for further investigations. He was a former smoker of 25 pack-years quitted 2 years ago before the presentation. He had end-stage renal disease requiring deceased donor kidney transplantation 4 years ago. After transplantation, he was on immunosuppressive agents, including mycophenolate mofetil and cyclosporine. Acyclovir was also prescribed for herpes infection prophylaxis.
He was referred to our hospital. Physical examination showed an asthenic patient with anicteric sclera. His vital signs revealed a body temperature of 38 c, blood pressure of 100/60 mm Hg, a pulse rate of 90/minute, and a respiratory rate of 17/minute. His oxygen saturation was 95% at ambient air. Respiratory examination revealed decreased breath sound at the left upper lung zone without crackles or egophony. Other physical examinations were unremarkable.
Complete blood count showed mild anemia with a hemoglobin level of 10.1 g/dL and leukocytosis with white blood cells count of 22 x 103/microL, 91% neutrophils. Blood chemistry tests remained within normal ranges. The chest radiograph (Figure 1A) and contrast-enhanced chest CT (Figure 1B) showed a large mass in the left upper lobe. A transthoracic core-needle biopsy of the left upper lobe mass was performed. The biopsy specimens were sent for pathological and microbiological studies. The histopathology revealed non-small cell carcinoma admixed with necrotic tissues. The immunohistochemical studies for cytokeratin (CK) AE1/AE3, CK7, and thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) were positive, compatible with primary lung adenocarcinoma. The Brown-Hopp stain revealed a single cluster of gram-negative bipolar rods with safety pin appearance characteristics of B. pseudomallei. (Figure 2A-D). B. pseudomallei subsequently grew on tissue culture. His serum antibody titer against B. pseudomallei was positive with a titer of 1:1280. His blood culture for aerobes and serum cryptococcal antigen were negative. The patient was finally diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (T4N0M0) co-existing with localized pulmonary melioidosis. The molecular analysis did not detect mutations of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) genes and the rearrangement of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene.
After 3 weeks of intravenous ceftazidime, his fever subsided, and his well-being improved. He gradually gained his weight. Oral co-trimoxazole was sequentially prescribed for 20 weeks after the completion of intravenous ceftazidime treatment. He underwent surgery for left thoracotomy and left upper lobectomy. However, the procedure was not accomplished due to severe adhesion surrounding the entire left lung and great vessels. After surgery, he received concurrent chemoradiation therapy with a paclitaxel-based regimen for adenocarcinoma. Nevertheless, he developed progression of disease soon after. Three cycles of palliative chemotherapy using pemetrexed were delivered. Unfortunately, he finally passed away after 2 years after the initial presentation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old Thai male farmer presented with a 3-month history of prolonged fever, non-productive cough, intermittent left chest tightness, and a 4 kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced prolonged fever, dry cough, intermittent left hemithorax tightness, and a 4 kg weight loss over 3 months. He had been admitted to a local hospital with a diagnosis of bacterial pneumonia, but his fever failed to resolve despite 14 days of intravenous meropenem, prompting referral to our hospital.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease status post deceased-donor kidney transplantation 4 years earlier, maintained on immunosuppressive therapy (mycophenolate mofetil and cyclosporine) and prophylactic acyclovir. Former smoker (25 pack-years, quit 2 years prior). Worked as a farmer in central Thailand.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prolonged fever, non-productive cough, intermittent left chest tightness, and 4 kg weight loss. Home medications: mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, and acyclovir.

objective.physical_examination: Asthenic build with anicteric sclerae. Vital signs: temperature 38 C, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, pulse rate 90/min, respiratory rate 17/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on ambient air. Respiratory examination revealed decreased breath sounds over the left upper lung zone without crackles or egophony; other systemic examinations were unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed mild anemia (hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL) and leukocytosis (WBC 22 x 10^3/microL with 91% neutrophils). Blood chemistry tests were within normal limits. Aerobic blood cultures and serum cryptococcal antigen were negative. Chest radiograph showed a large mass in the left upper lobe. Serum antibody titer against Burkholderia pseudomallei was positive at 1:1280.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced chest CT confirmed a large mass in the left upper lobe. Transthoracic core-needle biopsy of the left upper lobe mass demonstrated non-small cell carcinoma admixed with necrotic tissue on histopathology; immunohistochemistry was positive for CK AE1/AE3, CK7, and TTF-1 (confirming primary lung adenocarcinoma), while molecular testing was negative for EGFR mutations and ALK rearrangements. Brown-Hopps tissue staining revealed a cluster of bipolar-stained Gram-negative rods with a 'safety pin' appearance.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Stage IIIA primary lung adenocarcinoma (T4N0M0) co-existing with localized pulmonary melioidosis (tumor-to-infection collision lesion), confirmed by biopsy histopathology/immunohistochemistry (CK AE1/AE3+, CK7+, TTF-1+), Brown-Hopps staining, positive B. pseudomallei serology (1:1280), and lung tissue culture isolating Burkholderia pseudomallei. Management and clinical course: Treated with 3 weeks of intravenous ceftazidime (resulting in defervescence, improved well-being, and weight gain) followed by 20 weeks of oral co-trimoxazole eradication therapy. Left thoracotomy for planned left upper lobectomy was aborted due to dense adhesions involving the left lung and great vessels. He subsequently received paclitaxel-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by three cycles of palliative pemetrexed for progressive lung adenocarcinoma, and died 2 years after initial presentation.
